Neural Dual Contouring (NDC) was introduced as a data-driven mesh reconstruction method based on dual contouring that uses a neural network to predict vertex locations and edge crossings, eliminating the need for hand-crafted functions and surface gradients [S3].

The claim states that Neural Dual Contouring (NDC) is a data-driven mesh reconstruction method based on dual contouring, uses a neural network to predict vertex locations and edge crossings, and eliminates the need for hand-crafted functions and surface gradients. Source [S3] explicitly confirms all these points: it introduces NDC as a 'data-driven approach to mesh reconstruction based on dual contouring,' states that it 'uses a neural network to predict' vertex locations and edge crossings (or signs/crossings), and highlights that it does not require 'surface gradients' or 'hand-crafted functions' unlike classical DC.

Self-Supervised Dual Contouring (SDC) was later proposed as a variant that uses self-supervised losses relying only on the input SDF, avoiding dependence on vertex positions obtained via QEF minimization [S1].

The evidence explicitly states that Self-Supervised Dual Contouring (SDC) is a meshing framework that extends Neural Dual Contouring with self-supervised losses. It confirms that SDC relies only on the input SDF (specifically using sign changes for connectivity and self-supervised losses for vertex positions) and explicitly excludes dependence on vertex positions obtained via Quadratic Error Function (QEF) minimization, which is a requirement for standard Dual Contouring.
